And thirty-two years later, a new tower was built between the two towers.
And in the year 1475 [of the Greeks],
1475: the blessed Mor Michael built the southern tower.
And in the year ... he built a battlement (a corner tower?) for the upper fortress belonging to the monastery.
And in the year 459,
459 of the Arabs [1066-1067 AD]:
Gümüshtekin (Kümüshtekin), the commander of the Turks, marched against Edessa.
And the Duke of Edessa came out to meet him,
and he was defeated and also captured.
And for twenty thousand dinars he ransomed himself,
and entered Edessa again.
And Gümüshtekin took control of Harran, Sarug, and Callinicus.
And when (then) he turned back to go to Sultan Alp Arslan,
and reached Khilat,
he became enraged against one of the amirs who was with him and killed him.
Now this man had a brother whose name was Afshin,
and he went in to Gümüshtekin while he was drunk and killed him.
And he gathered for himself an army of the Turks,
and turned back and went to the region of Antioch,
taking captives and plundering.
And in this year, the niece of Bagrat, king of the Iberians of Abkhazia, was brought
as a wife for Sultan Alp Arslan;
and he celebrated her wedding in the city of Hamadan.
And after a little while he gave her a letter of divorce,
and gave her in marriage to one of the nobles.
And in the year 460,
460 of the Arabs [1067-1068 AD]:
A certain Armenian patrician whose name was Aristakes, when he came out of a certain fortress to go to another that was stronger than it,
out of fear of the Turks,
with two hundred men,
a certain Turkish amir whose name was Shirwanshah fell upon him.
And out of their fear the Armenians said:
"We are going to the Sultan to convert to Islam at his hands."
And so with honor they conducted them to the Sultan.
And unwillingly, they all converted to Islam and were circumcised.
And the Sultan gave to the patrician each year twenty thousand dinars as stipends.
And afterwards they fled to Inner Armenia,
and returned to their Christian faith.
And when Constantine Doukas, the emperor of the Romans, died,
Romanos, that is Diogenes, was made king.
